title: Serve a sitemap that conforms to the sitemap protocol schema
statement: Every published sitemap and sitemap index parses as XML, uses the protocol namespace, contains only the elements the protocol defines, and gives each entry a fully qualified URL rather than a path.
rationale: A file that fails to parse or uses an unrecognised namespace is rejected whole rather than partially, so a single malformed entry can discard the entire submission without any visible symptom on the site.
implementation: Generate the file from the route inventory rather than maintaining it by hand, escaping URL entities as the protocol requires. Validate the generated output against the schema as part of the build so a malformed entry fails before it is published.

verification.method: Fetch each published sitemap URL and parse the body against the protocol schema, recording the namespace, element names, and any parse failure.

caution: This control governs the sitemap a site publishes. Publishing one is not treated as mandatory here, because the documented guidance describes it as helpful for large or poorly linked sites rather than as a universal requirement.

title: Omit sitemap entries whose target suppresses indexing
statement: No sitemap entry names a URL that responds with a noindex directive or that a robots.txt rule disallows, so the file does not ask for processing of addresses the site has separately excluded.
rationale: Listing an excluded URL states two opposite intents at once, and the engine reports it as an error rather than choosing between them, which buries genuine coverage problems under contradictions the site created.
implementation: Filter the generator's input by the same indexability annotation the route inventory carries, so an entry cannot be emitted for a route marked excluded. Where the exclusion is wrong, change the annotation rather than adding the URL back to the sitemap by hand.

verification.method: For every sitemap entry, evaluate the robots.txt rules against it and read the robots directives from its response, listing the entries excluded by either.

title: Set lastmod from a real content modification timestamp
statement: The lastmod value of an entry comes from when the page's content last changed, in the W3C Datetime format the protocol specifies, and it does not move because the site was rebuilt or redeployed.
rationale: A timestamp that advances on every build carries no information about what changed, and once the values stop correlating with real edits they are discounted, which also discards the signal for the pages that genuinely did change.
implementation: Take the value from the content store - the CMS updated field, the commit date of the source file, or the record's own modified column. Do not fall back to the build time, and omit the element entirely when no reliable timestamp exists.

verification.method: Compare each entry's lastmod against the modification time recorded for that content, then rebuild without editing content and confirm the values did not move.

title: List sitemap URLs on the same host that serves the sitemap
statement: Entries name URLs on the host from which the sitemap was fetched, unless the sitemap is a cross-submission that the receiving platform has been told to accept for the other host.
rationale: The protocol scopes a sitemap to the location it is served from, so entries for another host fall outside that scope and are ignored rather than merely deprioritised.
implementation: Build entry URLs from the same configured origin the canonical uses, so a deployment serving several hosts produces a separate file per host. In a monorepo, generate one sitemap per deployed application rather than one combined file.

verification.method: Compare the host of every entry against the host that served the containing sitemap and list the mismatches.

title: Split sitemaps before the protocol size limits
statement: No single sitemap file exceeds the protocol's maximum of 50000 URLs or 50 MB uncompressed; larger inventories are divided into several files referenced from a sitemap index.
rationale: A file over either limit is rejected in full, so a growing site crosses the boundary silently and loses the whole submission at the moment the inventory is largest and the file matters most.
implementation: Have the generator chunk its output on entry count and byte size rather than assuming the inventory stays small, and emit an index whenever more than one file results. Keep the index itself within the same limits.

verification.method: Count the entries and measure the uncompressed byte length of every published sitemap file, including each child named by an index.

title: Regenerate the sitemap whenever the published URL set changes
statement: Adding, removing, or moving a public page updates the sitemap in the same operation, so the file never names URLs that no longer resolve or omits URLs that are already live.
rationale: A sitemap generated once and left alone becomes a list of the site as it used to be, and the stale entries consume the crawl the submission requests while the new pages it omits wait to be found by link discovery alone.
implementation: Generate the file during the build for a statically published site, or from the content store on request for a database-driven one. Where content is published without a rebuild, make publication trigger regeneration rather than relying on a scheduled job.

verification.method: Diff the entry set of the live sitemap against the current route and content inventory, reporting entries and routes present on only one side.
